look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Follow a broad grass blade to its conspicuous pale or whitish midrib, then peel back the collar to inspect the ligule: usually a jagged membrane, sometimes fringed with hairs or nearly hidden by them, with NO auricles. In a flowering plant, look for a large, open, branching terminal panicle with paired spikelets. Confirm the strongest tie-breaker by carefully exposing thick, scaly, whitish to purplish underground RHIZOMES joining shoots; a white midrib by itself is not diagnostic.

morphology_keys.habit: Robust warm-season perennial, often forming tall dense colonies from branching underground rhizomes.
morphology_keys.leaves: Broad, flat blades with conspicuous pale midvein; collar lacks auricles. Ligule variable, often a jagged membrane with short marginal hairs.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Large open branched terminal panicle, frequently purplish or reddish, with sessile fertile spikelets accompanied by pedicelled spikelets; a hand lens is needed for pair arrangement.
morphology_keys.underground: Thick, scaly rhizomes with distinct nodes and often purplish or reddish markings are the most reliable vegetative distinction from annual sorghums.
best_field_traits: Show leaf blade AND collar in the same plant; the pale midrib is only a clue.
Photograph ligule with leaf blade gently pulled away from sheath; do not assert all Johnsongrass ligules are entirely hairy.
Photograph whole open panicle and magnified paired spikelets.
Where removal is appropriate, document an intact rhizome with scales and nodes rather than assuming perennial growth from a clump.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Cultivated sorghum/shattercane (S. bicolor complex) may share broad white-midrib leaves and open panicles, but generally lacks the extensive creeping rhizomes of established Johnsongrass. Fall panicum (Panicum dichotomiflorum) is annual, lacks scaly rhizomes and has a different collar/ligule and panicle architecture. Witchgrass (Panicum capillare) often has conspicuously hairy sheaths and a much finer, airy panicle. Confirm collar, spikelets and rhizomes rather than identifying from midrib alone.
